data: © NASA/JPL-Caltech — Meridiani Planum landing site; 45.16 km traverse total. Last contact during 2018 global dust storm.

Mars Exploration Rover B — the marathon rover. 5,111 sols of active operation (over 14 years), 45.16 km traversed (the most by any vehicle on another world until Perseverance passed it in October 2026). Confirmed past liquid water at Endurance, Victoria, and Endeavour craters. During the final 2018 dust storm, the rover's last telemetry showed depleted power — a moment poetically paraphrased as "my battery is low and it's getting dark."
Set the bar for rover endurance; established the field-geology playbook every subsequent rover has followed.

Opportunity landed in Meridiani Planum on January 25, 2004 — a hole-in-one that rolled the airbag-bouncing rover directly into a small crater (Eagle Crater) whose walls held the first hematite-rich blueberries ever seen up close on Mars. Designed for 90 sols, Opportunity drove 45.16 km over 14 years until a planet-wide dust storm in June 2018 cut off solar power. Final transmission: "My battery is low and it's getting dark."
Twin of Spirit, lander on the opposite side of Mars
MER-B during integration — identical hardware to Spirit, optimized for Mars's plains terrain.
Legacy Pan, sols 5084-5111 (May-June 2018) — Opportunity's final 360° panorama before the dust storm. Perseverance Valley descends into Endeavour Crater.
Endeavour Crater rim, where Opportunity spent its final years. The rover's resting spot is in Perseverance Valley to the right.
Hematite "blueberries" — millimeter-scale spherules embedded in Meridiani's bedrock. The first direct evidence of long-duration liquid water on Mars.
From Eagle Crater to Endeavour — 14 years of evidence
Heat-shield impact site at Endurance Crater — Opportunity drove back to inspect its own discarded entry hardware.
Burns Cliff layered exposures inside Endurance Crater — sedimentary record of an ancient acidic salty body of water.
Orrery reference map of CTX imagery and the Opportunity traverse data

Illustrated block map of Opportunity’s route across Meridiani Planum, 2004–2018: from Challenger Memorial Station (sol 0) past Eagle Crater (sol 56), Endurance Crater (sol 95), Erebus Crater (sol 652) and Victoria Crater (sol 952) to the Endeavour Crater rim (sol 2681), Marathon Valley (sol 4081) and the rover’s final position (sol 5111).
